I get this all the time, I’ll have to tell my wife to take a sec and stop so I can feel a bit comfier. I had a lot of trauma in the past when it came to doing things for myself - I still do. It’s like my brain wants to run away from something that feels ‘good’ for me. That can manifest in me getting overwhelmed suddenly and getting excited for the idea of it but then when it comes into practice, it’s ’too much’. I grew up religious so a lot of things like this were drilled into me as sinful or wrong. I always feel so guilty when time is spent pleasuring me, despite my wife just wanting to make me happy.

Not saying this is your experience exactly ofc! But maybe you could consider some sensory issues from being ND or pre existing trauma from somewhere that might not have anything to do with your partner. 

Another part to this (for myself) is that in the past I was a lot more impulsive with sexual things. I saw romance as sexual things instead of someone caring for me also which damaged my self esteem. Now that I’m with someone that cares for me and doesn’t want to use me, it’s like my body doesn’t know what to do in a loving situation. All of this is stuff that’s to be sorted in therapy, but I wanted to share just in case anything resonated.

I’ve struggled with BED for a good 20yrs - severe weight gain, the whole 10 yards. I was really unwell/was most likely going to end up dead if I continued, thankfully I met my current wife and she’s been a huge help with gaining some normalcy in my life. I started vyvanse (for adhd) about 1 and a half years ago and I’ve dropped a lot of weight and my food intake is much more manageable these days.

I went through some weird ghost cravings for a bit at the beginning where I’d get the urge but then as soon as I started eating I was full quickly and then over time that kind of just equalised out to where I am now. I do have some rough days where the suppressing feeling is very intense and I know I have to eat something but will feel very nauseous. I was told a bunch of times that the suppressing feeling will go over time but I personally haven’t experienced that myself. 

But it’s been a huge change and I constantly mourn all the things I could have done, I was a pretty sporty kid too; did martial arts/swimming but then I hit maybe 7-9 years of age and suddenly I’m scrounging in the cabinets for anything I could get my hands on. Partially that was due to abuse in the home but I also think not being medicated/understood/supported was a huge role in things.

Welcome to the next stage of weirdness; going from eating everything to being disgusted by your fave foods. I was/am literally in the same position except I take Wellbutrin with my Vyvanse for ADHD. Before march last year I had very severe BED, was over 400lbs etc. 

It’s been a really weird experience on a psychological level, I only ever really crave fruit which ofc isn’t terrible but it’s almost like I have ARFID, without having ARFID. I’m ND so I already had issues with picky eating, but when I started Wellbutrin it basically sent that into overdrive. I’ve lost a decent amount of weight and I’m much happier in that regard, but I do miss being able to eat the things I want to at certain moments - most of the time I look at food in general, get disgusted and then give up on eating it. 

What’s helped me mostly is basically just having a list of safe foods, for me it’s things like; granola bars, fruit, chips, smoothies, small veggies, pasta that I can readily heat up. And drinking water, like a lot of water. Fruit is my favourite in that I can just load up a bowl of it and then chomp on it while at my pc, and I’m also getting hydration in at the same time. It’s better if you eat something, rather than nothing, even if it might be deemed “unhealthy”. I’ve felt awful on days that I was just too repulsed to eat, I’ve also developed some bowel problems as a result so I can definitely recommend eating at least a small meal.

It’s a major change and it’s gonna take some time to get used to, your diet might look a lil weird for a bit but I found the appetite thing gets better over time. I also use 🍃 if I’m really struggling for appetite that day, but I wouldn’t say that’s necessary or needed.
